name: volunteering
summary: Volunteers give their time to cleanups, food banks, events and good causes.
description: Organizers offer a spot to help, in person or online, and volunteers ask for one: cleanups, food banks, community events, nature, animal shelters, and remote help for a cause, such as translating or writing. Not a bed for help, which is stays-work, and not caring for children or for people who need care. In person it is for adults only, since strangers meet; online it is open to anyone.

description.description: The help, in the writer's words: in an offer, the cause, the tasks and what to bring; in a request, what the volunteer would like to do, and what they bring, such as a skill.

help.description: What the help is, and for nature and animals what it is for, every value that applies, such as translation and animals for translating an animal rescue's website; a cause no value names, such as refugees, goes in the description: cleanup is picking up litter, in parks, on beaches, by rivers or in streets; food is sorting, packing, cooking or handing out food, as at a food bank; events is setting up, running and clearing up community events, such as a fair, a race or a festival; nature is planting trees and caring for land and wildlife, litter apart; animals is helping animals, as at a shelter or a rescue; translation, writing and design are for a cause's papers, posts and posters; digital work is websites, social media and data.

mode.description: How the help is given: in person, online, or both.

place.description: Where the help is: in an offer, where volunteers meet, exact if it is a public spot such as a park gate or a food bank, else a circle round the area; in a request, anywhere in the circle the volunteer will go.

dates.description: When, for help on set days: in an offer, when it starts, or the span it runs, such as a cleanup from 10:00 to 13:00; in a request, the span the volunteer is free, such as while they are in town.

hours.description: When, for help every week: in an offer, the shifts, such as Saturdays from 9:00 to 12:00; in a request, when the volunteer is free each week.

weeklyHours.description: For help every week, how many hours a week: what the organizer asks, or what the volunteer gives, such as 5, or 2 to 4.

shiftHours.description: How long one shift lasts, or the shortest and the longest, such as 2 to 3.

volunteers.description: How many volunteers the organizer needs, in all or for each shift, the description saying which: such as 10, or the fewest and the most, such as 10 to 20, or at least 5.

people.description: How many come together, the volunteer included, such as 4 for a group of friends or coworkers.

languages.description: By ISO 639-1 code, such as en for English: in an offer, the languages spoken while helping, or those a translation is from and into; in a request, those the volunteer can help in.

photos.description: Photos of the place or of past help.

asDescribed.description: Whether the help was as the organizer's listing said: the tasks, the place and the times.

showedUp.description: Whether the volunteer came as agreed, online or in person: no if they missed it, or cancelled too late to plan around.

feltSafe.description: Whether the writer felt safe with them: no if anything made them uneasy; left out when they never met.
